title: Unassigned loop variable causes GPU and entire computer to crash
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.6.stable.arch_linux with Forward renderer
- Non-reproducible with Compatibility renderer

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable unknown - Manjaro Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 16 Feb 2026 21:35:51 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 550 / 550 Series (radeonsi, polaris12, ACO, DRM 3.64, 6.18.12-1-MANJARO) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.56 GiB memory

### Issue description

I was working on a shader and my entire computer froze, requiring me to hard-reboot it. It happened again every time I opened the scene with the shader, so I looked into it and tracked it down to this part:

`	for(int i;i<origin_amount;i++)`

Initializing the loop variable to 0 solves the issue. This line alone does not cause the problem, however, so it's a combination of the uninitialized variable and what I was doing with it in the rest of the shader.

I've attached the complete shader for reference, but I think the specifics of the problem are probably a Vulkan thing and cannot be solved from Godot. What _could_ be done to help, however, is to prevent shaders with uninitialized for loops from being compiled and run. That is, lines such as the one I wrote above should be considered syntax errors.

The problem is ultimately caused by my mistake of not initializing the variable, but it seems to me that it is an easy mistake to make and the consequences are grave enough (might cause loss of work) that it makes sense to put some safeguards like the one I propose.

I know very little about how the shader language works, however, so forgive me if this is not as trivial as I think it is or if it doesn't make sense at all.

### Steps to reproduce

Open the attached project. Open the only existing scene.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[shader-crash-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25570832/shader-crash-bug.zip)

WARNING: even opening this project might cause your system to freeze to the point where it requires a full restart. Make sure to save any unsaved changes before you try it.
